articleTitle: A Comparison of Various Solid-State Pulse Generators for Small-Scale Nonlinear Transmission Line Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: Printed circuit board (PCB) based dispersive non-linear transmission lines (NLTLs) require an electrical driver capable of delivering nanosecond to microsecond pulses up to 3 kV. The upper voltage limit of these devices is primarily constrained by the availability of high-quality factor components for the PCB-NLTL with the required voltage handling capacity. For this voltage range, many pulse generator options exist, and the characteristics of these pulse generators (complexity versus simplicity, cost, features, and capability, etc.) can vary widely among different topologies. This presentation reviews and quantitatively compares several pulse generator topologies that have been developed for use with PCB-NLTLs and experimentally characterized into both a 50 Ohm dummy load and a PCB-NLTL load.

articleTitle: Spark Gap Impedance Collapse and Current Rise Times in Modern Insulating Gas Mixtures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: This work tests 100% N2, SF6, and C4F7N (Novec™ 4710) at pressures ranging from 0.5 to 3 atm, using a gap distance of 2.2 mm. The coaxial spark gap is impedance matched on both the anode and cathode side and enables the measurement of breakdown events with single-digit nanosecond temporal resolution. Custom diagnostics have been fabricated and characterized with a bandwidth greater than or equal to 600 MHz capable of measuring voltages and currents of several 100 kV and few kA. The impedance collapse of spark gaps operated with different gas mixtures at various pressures is critical to understanding the pulsed limitations of an apparatus. Experiments have revealed that, in a 2.2 mm coaxial gap at pressures greater than or equal to 1.5 atm, pure Novec™ 4710 (C4F7N) has improved switching characteristics when compared to pure SF6.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of the Upper Frequency Limits of a PCB-based Nonlinear Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: This study focused on the impact of line length, or number of stages, on the RF performance of lumped-element NLTL PCBs, showing that comparable RF performance can be achieved by NLTLs with as few as 20 discrete stages if a HV driver is used with a fast enough fall-time. Additionally, higher operating frequencies were achieved by lowering the discrete inductance and capacitance values used in the NLTL, but these higher-frequency waveforms contained lower RF energy than the lower-frequency NLTL PCBs with the same number of stages and the same input pulse voltages.

articleTitle: Study on the Effect of Nanosecond Pulsed Electric Fields (nsPEFs) on Cancer Tumors in Embryonic Chick Assay
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: Currently, cancer is a major cause of death worldwide. The major treatment methods for cancer as surgical treatment, radiation therapies, and drug therapy have the disadvantages of physically demanding on the patient, the risk of radiation exposure, and strong side effect. Therefore, this study aims to establish a new cancer treatment method using pulsed power to reduce these disadvantages. As basic research for establishing the cancer treatment method using pulsed power, we applied nanosecond pulsed electric fields (nsPEFs) to cancer cell suspensions (EMT6) to investigate the effect of cell death and induction of apoptosis. The pulse width, electric field strength, and number of applied pulses were changed, and cell viability after 24 hours of application and apoptosis after 3 hours and 24 hours of application was measured in this experiment. From the results on the cell suspension, we also applied nsPEFs on solid tumors developed on the chorioallantonic membrane of chicken eggs by using the embryonic chick assay. The solid tumors removed from the eggs and their masses were measured three days later after nsPEFs application. The shape of the electrodes applied nsPEFs on solid tumors was investigated. In the experiments with cell suspensions, the cell viabilities decreased and apoptosis was detected in some conditions. In the experiments of application to tumors, as the applied voltage and the number of applied pulses increased, the mass of tumors tended to decrease. Differences in mass of tumor were also observed depending on the shape of the electrodes. However, the significant differences by application of nsPEFs were not observed because of experimental techniques.

articleTitle: Modular kW-Class Pulsed Power Capacitor Charger for High Frequency Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: Spiral generators have been proven as an effective way to generate high voltages on the nanosecond scale in a compact size. In their open state, they act as an electrostatic energy storage device, but when closed quickly they can become a voltage multiplier and an RF source. When storing energy, they function similarly to a capacitor by storing voltage across their dielectric layers. To operate spiral generators in a repeated pulsed manner, a specific kind of pulsed capacitor charger is used. These pulsed power capacitor chargers come in very many forms and have extensive utilization on the market. However, most existing systems sacrifice size and weight to increase pulsed power output. This paper focuses specifically on the design and development of a compact, power dense, pulsed power supply to be integrated with a compact spiral generator. The design centers around a single full-bridge DC-DC converter on an individual PCB that can be modularly connected to other identical converters, increasing power output. At their input the converters are connected in parallel, allowing for current sharing between the boards. On the output the boards are connected in series, stacking the output voltages in reference to each other. The final system assembly is designed and built to utilize four individual converter PCBs connected together. Each individual DC-DC converter uses gallium-nitride (GaN) switches and a planar transformer to maximize power density. Operation of the modular power supply assembly is experimentally shown to charge a 0.47 μF load capacitor to 1625 V at a pulse repetition frequency of 30 kHz. This charge sequence is demonstrably repeated up to 300 times in a 9.3 ms window, with an 81% energy efficiency, which is a 33% efficiency improvement over traditional capacitor bank and closing switch circuitry. The system reaches peak output power levels of 64.3 kW and an average power of 21.4 kW all within a 36 in<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> volume, resulting in a power density of 1786 W/in<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. Specific discussion on the converter design, modularity, configurability, and scalability will be presented.

articleTitle: Blumlein-Generator with a GaN-HEMT in gate-boosted Operation as Closing Switch
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: Gate-boosted operation of a GaN-HEMT allows for an operation with a rise time significantly faster than listed in the data sheet. For a GaN-HEMT having a rise time of approximately 4 ns under normal operating conditions a rise time of less than 1 ns in gate-boosted operation has been demonstrated. The employed gate boosting circuit compensates for the inductance in the gate circuit and the voltage drop across the inductance in the source path of the GaN-HEMT in such a way that the resonant frequency of the input circuit increases significantly and the gate can be charged more quickly. The voltage reduction due to the resulting capacitive voltage divider formed by the added series capacitor and the input capacitance of the GaN-HEMT is compensated by a sufficiently high driver voltage. A three-stage Marx circuit equipped with avalanche-rated bipolar transistors as closing switches has been used as voltage source for the driver. The gate-boosted GaN-HEMT has been tested as switch in a Blumlein configuration set up with 50-Ohm-cables as transmission lines. The contribution describes selected design details and presents measurement results obtained with the described test setup.

articleTitle: Inhibition of Conversion Myoglobin to Metmyoglobin in Red Fish Meat by Applying Pulsed High Electric Field
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: The temperature must be kept at -50°C or less by using an ultra-low temperature freezer to store, cut, and transport meats because this suppresses the color change of the meats. Therefore, meat prices become high. The color change of the meats is caused by that myoglobin converts to metmyoglobin by the decomposition of ATP. The decomposition of ATP, which is a freshness indicator of meats, caused by ATPase that is a decomposition enzyme of ATP. If ATPase could be deactivated, the long-term storage would be possible in a general-purpose refrigerator because the meat color does not change at -18°C. Therefore, we considered the application of pulsed power technology to deactivate ATPase. Pulsed high electric field has been reported to be able to suppress enzyme activity without thermally impact to targets depending on pulse conditions. In this presentation, bonito red fish meat was used for a sample applying the pulsed high electric field, because it undergoes a noticeable color change over a short period of time. Furthermore, since it has been reported that myoglobin is easier to become metmyoglobin at between -5°C and -10°C, the bonito red fish meats were stored in a freezer set at -6°C after applying the pulsed high electric field. Then, the change in color of the bonito red fish meat and the rate of conversion from myoglobin to metmyoglobin for the elapsed time were investigated. As a result, it is found that application of the pulse high electric field can suppress the conversion myoglobin to metmyoglobin in the bonito red fish meat.

articleTitle: Recirculating-Flow Aqueous Electrolyte Resistor*
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: Cooling and temperature control are necessary in order to utilize an aqueous-electrolyte resistor as a high-power load for testing repetitively pulsed power systems. We describe a recirculating-flow system with a reservoir volume of 24 liters and maximum flow rate of 17.8 liters/minute. The electrolyte solution may be cooled or heated by a secondary coolant loop and two spiral heat exchangers. Thermal transfer is from electrolyte solution to coolant (distilled water) to air, therefore the operating point of the electrolyte solution must be above ambient air temperature. Temperature regulation better than ±0.2 C is maintained for a 350-W load as long as the solution temperature is at least 10 C than ambient. Higher power loads are possible with warmer solutions. The system easily satisfies the design goal of a maximum temperature excursion of 1.8 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex> for the dummy load employed with the Sirius I prototype system.

articleTitle: The Upgrade of the SNS Extraction Kicker Power Supplies for the Proton Power Upgrade
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: The Proton Power Upgrade (PPU) project at the Spallation Neutron Source (SNS) aims to enhance the linear accelerator's power output from 1.4 to 2.8 megawatts. A critical focus lies on upgrading the Extraction Kicker Power Supplies to handle the amplified beam power. The existing capacitor charging power supplies lacked the capability to charge the Blumlein-type Pulse Forming Network (PFN) to the required 40 kV at a repetition rate of 60 Hz. To address this limitation, an initial solution involving the use of a resonant charging circuit was proposed. However, a challenge arose with a self-firing issue in the thyristor switch, which proved unsolvable within the given timeframe. Facing a critical decision point in the project, an alternative approach was explored: integrating a supplementary power supply to enhance the overall power capacity. This solution was tested and ultimately chosen as the path forward. To accommodate the additional power supply, the power distribution system had to undergo upgrades. Throughout this endeavor, a comprehensive examination of the system took place, with meticulous identification of key components. This paper delves into the technical challenges encountered during the process and the corresponding solutions that were implemented.

articleTitle: New Generation Energy Extraction Systems for the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider Project at CERN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: A new, high-speed, and high-current DC switching technology based on commercial medium-voltage vacuum interrupters was explored and successfully validated for future use in the energy extraction systems (EES) to protect the superconducting magnet circuits at CERN. In the development process, two types of systems were produced, one rated for 2 kA and another for 600 A. Alongside the tests and validation of the prototype and pre-series, an upgrade of the design involving the control and power-electronic circuits and topology took place to ensure adequate redundancy and higher reliability of the equipment. The whole process required additional R&D work and an extensive test program, the positive outcome of which affirmed the vacuum switch solution as a baseline design for the future EES foreseen to protect several superconducting magnet circuits of the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider (HL-LHC) project. The final design demonstrated the desired performance and paved the way for industrial series production. This paper gives an overview of the entire project and discusses the additional development and improvement of the control and power electronics. It presents the basic properties of the vacuum-switch-based energy extraction systems, as well as some operational aspects.

articleTitle: Liquid Nanodielectrics for Heat Transfer in 3D Heterogeneous Microsystems: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: Three-dimensional heterogeneous integrated (3DHI) circuits can be made by stacking layers of microsystems one over the other and making the connection shorter, which allows for less power consumption since the DC losses will be very low over shorter distances. This novel and innovative packing technique of the microsystems was considered revolutionary in achieving 100% packing efficiency, compactness, and low power consumption. However, the thermal management issues that are imminent to the internal processing components in the 3DHI limit the widespread implementation of this technology. Although the two-phase heat transfer significantly enhances the heat removal from the micro and nano-sized passages, the complexity arises when the coolant comes in direct contact with the electrically active components. The best way to counter this problem is by using fluids that have dielectric properties. However, these dielectric liquids are invariably known for their poorer thermal conductivity and physical properties than water. So, the thermal properties of these liquids need to be enhanced to be used in place of the existing coolants. One way to do that is by adding nanoparticles, which have been proven to enhance the thermal conductivity of fluids significantly. Using nanodielectric fluids (NDFs) as a coolant in the 3DHI of microsystems can be a convincing alternative to the existing thermal management techniques that use water (or other electrically conducting liquids) as a coolant. This paper critically reviews the existing NDFs studied in power transformers to provide enhanced heat dissipation and dielectric strength to propose potential NDF options for 3DHI systems. This can be a transformative and innovative approach to thermal management in microsystems.

articleTitle: Thermal Characterization of GaN Switches in Pulsed Power Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: In this work, a method is presented for modeling Gallium-Nitride (GaN) semiconductor devices for the purpose of predicting junction temperature of devices experiencing high thermal transients in pulsed power applications. This work focuses on using the Cauer RC thermal network model published within the device datasheet to make these predictions. A Cauer RC model is constructed within a SPICE environment and a results matrix is presented for multiple operating cases. A transient finite-element heat transfer model is also presented for a fine wire thermocouple to predict the transient temperature response of the traditional contact temperature measurement. Multiple cases are presented, predicting as much as a 45 °C error between peak device junction temperature and thermocouple output.

articleTitle: Calculation of Radio Interference for Unconventional High Surge Impedance Loading Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: It is crucial to study the effects of corona discharge during the design of an overhead transmission line. These effects include power losses, radio interference (RI), television interference (TVI), and audible noise (AN). Extra high voltage conventional transmission lines above 300 kV are designed to have more than one conductor per phase to form conductor bundles which causes the electric field stress on the subconductors to be reduced, which in turn reduces the corona effects. Conventional high surge impedance loading (HSIL) lines consist of a higher number of subconductors with a larger bundle radius which effectively increases its transmission capacity. On the other hand, unconventional HSIL lines have demonstrated the potential to deliver higher natural power which surpasses that of both conventional and conventional HSIL lines. The term unconventional refers to the asymmetrical arrangement of the subconductors in bundles. With the increased number of subconductors per bundle, HSIL lines may have higher electric field stress on the conductors' surface leading to greater corona effects. In this paper, the RI from unconventional lines are evaluated and analyzed.

articleTitle: Simulation of Nanocrystalline Magnetic Cores Using Maxwell Ansys
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: Modeling magnetic core saturation has been of interest for various pulsed power topologies, such as those using linear transformer drivers (LTD). An extensive 3D Finite Element Method (FEM) analysis of FINEMET cores using Maxwell ANSYS is presented, aiming to align the computational model closely with experimental results obtained under varying magnetization rates obtained with voltage pulses of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 10$</tex> nanosecond rise times and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 1$</tex> microsecond duration. The study aims to elucidate the experimentally well-known widening effect of the hysteresis curve under high-frequency or pulse applications by exploring a range of model parameters, such as core conductivity, solid vs. laminations, etc., that best match the experiment. The more successful approach employs the concept of “effective conductivity” <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\sigma_{\text{eff }})$</tex> to simulate the hysteresis shift away from a DC curve in the magnetic core due to eddy currents in the core accompanied by ohmic core losses. While this specific method does not resolve laminations, it relies on adjusting <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma_{\text{eff }}$</tex> to closely match the experimental hysteresis curve for a base set of magnetization rate data. An effective conductivity value of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 10 \mathrm{S} / \mathrm{m}$</tex> using a solid core approximation reasonably matched that of an experimental laminated FT-3KL core with the pure magnetic material at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$833 \text{kS} / \mathrm{m}$</tex> conductivity. A thin oxide layer of insulation between laminations assumed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.001 ~\mathrm{S} / \mathrm{m}$</tex>. Keeping all simulation core properties constant, the widening of the BH curve for higher magnetization rates is reproduced in the simulation, facilitating a direct comparison with the experimental data over a broader range.

articleTitle: Multi-Output Capability in Helical Flux Compression Generators with Novel Inductive Seeding and Load Power Delivery
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: A novel Flux Compression Generator (FCG) configuration has been devised to overcome the inherent limitation of single output generation in traditional FCG systems. This advanced scheme enables the FCG to effectively drive loads requiring multiple outputs, significantly enhancing its application scope. The heart of the system is the Helical Flux Compression Generator (HFCG), which is indirectly seeded by a seed coil. The HFCG design is a refined multipitch variant based upon the work of Holt et. Al and Young et al. [1]–[4]. In this iteration the armature diameter is scaled to two inches with a stator to armature ratio of approximately 2. This empirical ratio for aluminum mitigates armature fracturing. An extensive simulation workflow was developed to assess and optimize this system. This process began with a detailed 2D axisymmetric Ansys Maxwell simulation encompassing all relevant inductances within the system. These calculated inductances are further integrated into a custom spice simulation specifically tailored to evaluate and refine the performance of multi-output multi-pitch HFCG designs. Encompassing the experiment, design, and simulation to achieve a multi-output multi-pitch HFCG allows for a broader application scope and furthered advancement in explosive pulsed power systems.

articleTitle: A Modular Pulser Test Bed for Characterization of Solid-State Opening Switches
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: Solid state switching and magnetic pulse compression are leveraged to create a modular test bed for characterization of Semiconductor Opening Switches (SOS) diodes. Capable of generating up to 70 kV pulses at 1 kA the pulser is used to drive trial SOS diodes and characterize these devices. A modular stack of saturable pulse transformers and secondary capacitance is used to vary the voltage multiplication ratio from the primary storage capacitance to the secondary resonant circuit. The circuit forward pumps the diode and charges the secondary capacitance whereby after the transformer is saturated the capacitor discharges on the negative swing and the SOS diode snaps shut to generate a fast-rise pulse. The modular test bed is used for testing series or parallel stacks of diodes in various configurations with swappable storage and transformer elements. Primary switching is achieved via commercial high-voltage thyristors with high dI/dt and low conduction losses.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Gas Insulation Within a Simulated Helical Flux Compression Generator Geometry Using Air, Sf6, and Novec 4710
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: In order to gain a deeper understanding of how well Novec <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${ }^{\text{TM }} 4710 (\mathrm{C}_{3} ~\mathrm{F}_{7} \text{CN})$</tex> would work as a substitute for sulfur hexafluoride <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{SF}_{6})$</tex> in helical flux compression generator (HFCG) applications, a comparative analysis was made between the relative dielectric breakdown properties of air, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SF}_{6}$</tex>, and Novec 4710 under the extreme conditions encountered in an HFCG. An experimental apparatus that emulated a helical FCG geometry was developed to allow the measurement of a time-resolved gas resistance using biased wire probes inserted into the device. After initiation, the expanding armature causes interplay between the advancing shocked gas region, armature, and the biased wire probes on the microsecond time scale. This leads to eventual dielectric breakdown on a nanosecond time scale. Incorporating piezoelectric pins, shorting pins, and fiber optic time-of-arrival sensors enabled precise tracking of the armature's position and the shock layer's progression, providing a measure of shock layer thickness at critical points. The spatial relationship between the shocked gas region, armature, and wire probes at the moment of breakdown was used to evaluate the relative performance of the different gases. The results demonstrate that Novec <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${ }^{\text{TM }}$</tex> 4710s performance closely aligns with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SF}_{6}$</tex>, indicating it may be a viable alternative to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SF}_{6}$</tex> in HFCG applications.

articleTitle: Construction of Mechanical-Electrical Combined Load Partial Discharge Measurement System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: Power semiconductors are advancing towards high voltage and high temperature operation, and their corresponding modules, composed of layered different materials, require designs able to resist high electric field and thermal stress at the material interface. Conventional reliability tests that simulate temperature cycle (T/C) environments, test separately electrical and mechanical properties, making it difficult to identify the cause of failure. This paper presents a new system that applies mechanical and electrical loads for real-time monitoring of partial discharge (PD) and delamination, which reveals the main reason for failure.

articleTitle: A New Topology for 2D Transmission-Line Array Circuit Simulations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: Complex or asymmetrical geometries can be difficult to model using ordinary, 1D, circuit modelling techniques. Simulating these geometries using 2D or 3D FDTD (Finite Difference Time Domain) tools is one solution, but is time consuming to implement, perform, and integrate into a larger circuit. 2D arrays of transmission lines have been used in these situations to give results similar to FDTD but in a much easier and faster way to implement, perform, and integrate into a larger circuit [1]. The existing technique for implementing 2D arrays, the 2D-TLM method [2], is to use a rectangular grid of transmission line elements. One issue with the usual TLM approach is that the impedance and transit time of the individual transmission line elements have to be scaled by the square root of two in order to get the correct behavior. A major problem with this is that the high frequency response of the array is not the same as the 1D representation of a TL element. A new topology for 2D transmission line arrays has been newly developed, known as the Chain Link Fence (CLF) topology. This topology is similar to a rectangular grid that has been rotated by 45 degrees. With the CLF topology, the individual transmission line elements have impedance and transit time values that do not need the square root of two scaling to get the correct response. A major benefit to the CLF topology is that the high frequency response of the array is exactly the same as the 1D representation. The circuit simulation tool, CASTLE [3], compares the TLM and CLF 2D array topologies against the results of FDTD simulations. These results are used to evaluate the CLF as an improved replacement for the grid topology for 2D transmission line array simulations of complex or asymmetrical geometries.

articleTitle: Alternative Encapsulation Material Combined with Geometric Techniques for Electric Field Mitigation Within (U)WBG Packages Under High Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: As power modules based on (U)WBG materials gain attention for their potential to revolutionize high-voltage, high-power density applications, their optimal performance is hindered by current insulation materials. The high electric field stress at triple points (TPs) and encapsulant's diminishing breakdown field strength at high temperatures significantly limit the application of power modules to below 200°C. Therefore, alternative encapsulation materials are essential for hightemperature applications. This paper proposes a novel solution involving replacing standard silicone gel (SG) encapsulant with high-temperature encapsulation composites created by integrating micro- and nano-sized fillers into a silicone elastomer matrix. Additionally, the ceramic structure is redesigned into a mesa configuration, featuring a trench at the base of the metal electrodes. The results from modeling and simulation of COMSOL Multiphysics demonstrate that this combined approach significantly reduces field stress at TPs. Although effective at lower frequencies, further design modifications, such as altering the metalized substrate into a protruding structure, are necessary for optimal electric field mitigation at frequencies above 10 kHz. This research addresses the critical issues of high electric field values at TPs and the limited temperature tolerance of current encapsulation materials, which are challenges exacerbated under high-frequency square pulse operation. By resolving these issues, this work represents a valuable advancement in utilizing highvoltage, high-power density (U)WBG power modules at demanding frequency environments.

articleTitle: Comparison of Inductive Generators (IG) built on Common Magnetic Core and Separate Cores
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: High-voltage power supplies (HVPS) for dc and long-pulse operation for a range of tens to several hundred kV are often built as cascade generators (CG). CGs can be roughly divided into two categories, those with capacitive and inductive energy coupling between the cascades. We will call here CGs with inductive coupling “Inductive Cascade Generators” (IG). Between several IG available topologies, two have been a matter of contention for decades: a) built on a common core; b) built in modules employing identical separate cores. The main argument against scheme b) is redundant insulation required to insulate the secondaries from the yokes, and the strong argument for it is the possibility of interleaving the modules for achieving low stored energy, fast dynamics, etc. This paper compares the two topologies based on core losses and cooling in practical configurations using U-cores. Both analytical and numerical thermal analyses are done. The first assumes constant volumetric losses, whereas the second uses core losses determined both by flux density and temperature in coupled magnetic field-thermal analyses. The losses for thermals are determined with Steinmetz approximations. While there is no universal preference for one or the other IG scheme, the derived dependencies can facilitate the choice between them accounting for the operational scenarios. For instance, there is a clear-cut preference for separate cores if high average power and fast dynamics are required at a very high output voltage.

articleTitle: Study on Selection of Appropriate Conditions of Nanosecond Pulsed Electric Field for Activation of Unfolded Protein Response Using GFP-Expressing Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) is under stress from the effects of various external and internal factors. It has been reported that the unfolded protein response (UPR) is activated by the application of nanosecond pulsed electric fields (nsPEFs). However, the nsPEFs conditions suitable for maximal UPR activity may vary depending on the target cell line. The purpose of this study is to select appropriate nsPEFs conditions for UPR activation using the Blumlein pulse forming line (B-PFL). The 293A cells are human fetal kidney cells that have been transfected to express Green fluorescent protein (GFP) upon UPR activation. Fluorescence intensity measurement and fluorescence observation of GFP produced 24 hours after application of nsPEFs were performed to estimate the activation level of UPR. Cell viability was also measured. Fluorescence intensity was found to increase under nsPEFs conditions compared to sham-applied samples. In particular, 65 nsPEFs (30 kV/cm, 80 shots) showed a significant difference in fluorescence intensity. The activation of the nsPEFs-induced UPR is not dependent on pulse width alone, but rather on the action of several parameters. This result suggests that the activation of the UPR by nsPEFs is maximal near the conditions that initiate the transition to cell death.

articleTitle: Development of a Custom Spiral Generator Winding Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: Spiral generators are pulsed-power devices than can produce high-voltage pulses in an ultra-compact form factor. The spiral generator acts as energy storage device, voltage multiplier, and RF source all in one system. A slower input charge is converted to a high voltage pulse on the order of hundreds of nanoseconds in pulse width. The construction is typically comprised of two conductive foils that are separated by dielectric films that are then wound in a spiral around a cylindrical core. The spiral generator's electrical characteristics are controlled directly through the geometry of the material stack and core size. While historically initiated using spark gaps as closing switches, the advancement of solid-state switching devices, such as SiliconCarbide (SiC) transistors, has enabled spiral generators to become completely solid-state. This improves repetition rate and jitter by several orders of magnitude. Since the holdoff voltage of solidstate switches is much lower than that of plasma switches, the charge voltage, and therefore the output voltage, is lower. The output voltage and power may be increased by adding turns and/or increasing the capacitance by using ultra-thin dielectric films. Ultra-thin films present many challenges to handling and integrating into the spiral generator. Significant care must be taken to ensure desired characteristics are achieved and not altered by wrinkles, dust, misalignment, and film quality. Mechanical accuracy and robustness of the spiral winding machinery becomes critical to realize uniform transmission line impedance and prevent voltage breakdown between layers. A custom spiral generator winding machine has been constructed to improve the overall spiral generator manufacturing process across a span of materials, down to dielectric films as thin as 0.3 mil. The machine incorporates features to improve the manufacturing process, such as laser film alignment, tension controlled bobbins, and integrated control panel. The bobbins can handle material spools and manage tension control with widths from 2 to 18 inches. The design considerations and improvements to spiral generator performance will be discussed.

articleTitle: Transient Simulations in Silvaco Victory Device for a N-Type SiC Drift Step Recovery Diode
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: This paper builds upon previous research in developing a SiC Drift Step Recovery Diode (DSRD) Model in Silvaco Victory Device. For this research, the DSRD is based on an N-type substrate for improved manufacturability. The model described in this paper was developed by characterizing DSRD devices under DC and transient conditions. The details of the pulsed power testbed developed for the transient characterization is outlined in this paper. The goal of this model is to allow the rapid development of future pulsed power systems and for further device structure optimization.

articleTitle: Prototyping Aircraft MVDC Power Cables with Optimal Multilayer Multifunctional Electrical Insulation Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: Emerging cable technologies play a vital role in the development of electric power systems (EPS) for wide-body all-electric aircraft (AEA), supporting improved power transmission with lower system mass. Although higher voltage levels contribute to enhanced power density, they also pose unique challenges in aircraft cable design. These challenges include suppressing arcing, handling partial discharge (PD) phenomena, and achieving reliable thermal management. Integrating multilayer multifunctional electrical insulation (MMEI) in aircraft cables offers a promising solution, as it helps reduce cable dimensions and weight. This method requires the selection of advanced materials tailored to specific performance needs. Our earlier studies addressed the modeling and simulation of MMEI-based MVDC power cables tailored to AEA system demands. However, validating the insulation performance and longevity of these designs under real conditions is critical. A thorough assessment of MMEI-configured power cables through experimental testing helps confirm their viability. This work focuses on a prototyping strategy for MVDC cables using various MMEI layer arrangements, highlighting the importance of optimizing production techniques to ensure cable consistency, eliminate faults, and prepare reliable test samples.

articleTitle: Design and Development of a Gate Drive Power Supply for Solid State Pulsed Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: The advancement of wide bandgap (WBG) semiconductors, such as silicon carbide (SiC) and gallium nitride (GaN), has enabled the development of solid-state driven pulsed power systems aimed at delivering higher efficiency and reliability compared to conventional pulsed power systems. Solid-state systems inherently allow for higher pulse repetition frequencies (PRF) to be achieved, further enhancing their versatility and applicability across various domains. However, driving the switching devices at speeds comparable to conventional systems poses a significant challenge. This article explores the design and development of a compact discontinuous conduction mode (DCM) flyback DC-DC converter tailored for three crucial application specifications. The first is supporting the higher gate drive power delivery due to increased PRF of the pulsed power system. The second is satisfying the higher output voltage requirement, which from prior literature shows an ability to improve switching speed of the SiC switches. The third is meeting isolation and EMI compliance for the power supply to help protect other sensitive electronics from noise generated from the pulsed power events on the secondary side. This design is experimentally demonstrated with a 1.73 in<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> circuit card assembly (CCA) that produces 175 V and 12 V output voltage, 25 W output power, 3000 V isolation, and < 15 pF of isolation capacitance.

articleTitle: Investigation on the Enhancement of Effects at Small Pulse Application Number on Sterilization of Packaged Cut Vegetables Using Pulsed Plasma under Usual and Low Oxygen Concentrations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: Even after packaging cut vegetables in a bag, it can be sterilized by generated active species by pulsed plasma produced in the bag by applying pulsed voltage to the package, and the risk of bacterial contamination is reduced. Currently, when the cut vegetables are packaged in the bag, in many cases, some oxygen gas is replaced by nitrogen gas to keep the vegetables freshness, and the inside of the bag is kept hypoxic. However, under hypoxic conditions, both the generation of ozone by pulsed plasma and its direct sterilizing efficacy are concurrently reduced. While the inactivation effect can be improved by increasing the number of pulsed applied, it concurrently amplifies damage to the vegetables. Therefore, this study aims to validate an efficient method of sterilizing packaged cut vegetables with fewer pulses under controlled atmosphere (CA) conditions.

articleTitle: Experimental Characterization of Distributed Ferromagnetic Nonlinear Transmission Lines in Different Geometries
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: This paper discusses ferromagnetic nonlinear transmission lines (NLTLs) that exhibit unique characteristics to tune and optimize high power microwave (HPM) generation. Similar studies on larger-scale NLTLs required excitation voltages in excess >10 kV. Alternatively, this research details a design that is compatible with printed circuit boards based pulsed power drivers, capable of delivering 1–3 kV high voltage excitation and pulse widths ranging from a few nanoseconds to microseconds. Distributed ferromagnetic NLTLs in a coaxial and stripline geometry are explored and characterized for the ability to generate moderate RF power output in the range of 100 MHz - 2.5 GHz range. Output power, frequency, and pulse duration are characterized for varying applied voltage, bias field, and ferrite materials. Based on these findings, it indicates that this novel geometry could be implemented into a modular phased array.

articleTitle: Testing and Qualification of Hermetically Sealed DC Contactors as Switching Elements in 600 Adc Energy Extraction Systems in Superconducting Circuits in the Large Hadron Collider Installations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: In the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) at CERN, 234 superconducting magnet circuits are protected by so-called Energy Extraction systems. The 606 customized Electro-Mechanical Circuit Breakers (EMCB) of the Energy Extraction Systems installed in circuits up to maximum 600 A, come to the theoretical end-of-life in the period 2026–2030. In the search for alternative switching elements, Hermetically Sealed DC contactors (HSDC) are considered as a reliable replacement. They need to provide a DC current carrying capability of at least 600 A, an opening-time of less than 20 ms and a power-cycle lifetime duration of more than 2000 cycles during a maintenance free operation period of minimum 10 years. Over the last 3 years, an extensive research program took place to test and qualify commercially-off-the-shelf available HSDC contactors. This paper presents the R&D program and the final results obtained on different brands and types of Hermetically Sealed DC-Contactors as well as the switching and arcing process in the typical Energy Extraction applications in high inductance circuits.

articleTitle: Thermal Models for Power IGBTs in Pulsed Power Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: We are reporting on thermal models for Power IGBTs used in Pulsed Power Applications. We are looking at Silicon (Si) IGBTs for Inverters used in Charging Power Supplies for Capacitors. We are modeling Si Power IGBTs using newly released device models in LTspice. From the results we can distinctly identify IGBT conduction losses, switching losses and diode losses. We modeled the accumulated energy loss into the base plate of one of our IGBT modules and calculated the associated temperature rise without an attached heat sink. We were able to validate the results with experimental data using measurements from an NTC (Negative Temperature Coefficient) thermistor mounted on the heat sink of the IGBT module. We added a ladder network to the simulation model that represents the transient thermal resistance of the IGBT given in the datasheet. That allows us to estimate the transient temperature inside the devices.

articleTitle: Characterization of the Dielectric Behavior of an Anodized Aluminum Plasma Chamber in a Plasma-Electrode Pockels Cell
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: A plasma-electrode Pockels cell (PEPC) [C. D. Boley and M. A. Rhodes, “Modeling of plasma behavior in a plasma-electrode Pockels cell,” IEEE Trans. Plasma Sci., vol. 27, no. 3, pp. 713–726, 1999] has been characterized to determine the dielectric and electric behavior of its anodized aluminum plasma chamber. The PEPC is an electro-optical component that utilizes two plasma channels as electrodes to apply a switching voltage across a large-aperture Pockels cell. The plasma channels are developed with a high-voltage, high-current electrical pulse into an anodized aluminum chamber filled with low-pressure helium gas. An anodization layer is added to prevent the plasma channel from developing an electrical arc to the conductive aluminum chamber. Poor anodization quality can often result in dielectric breakdowns, which not only disrupts the desired plasma pulse shape but also reduces the PEPCs lifetime and optical performance. The plasma and aluminum chamber's electrical behavior has been evaluated using an oscilloscope and high-bandwidth voltage probes and current monitors. The resulting data have been used to determine the quality of the anodized aluminum and its dielectric performance. This will guide engineering efforts to mitigate dielectric breakdown without sacrificing optical characteristics. Successful mitigation of dielectric breakdown will increase the efficiency and lifetime of existing and future PEPC systems.

articleTitle: Diagnosing Failure Mechanisms in Capacitors Within Pulsed Power Usage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: To provide the necessary energy to supply pulsed power operations, capacitors are most frequently used to store and release the necessary energy. Within these short durations of pulse triggering, the capacitors undergo high amounts of stress and begin to deteriorate through repeated usage. It is important to understand and diagnose the failure mechanisms that occur within the capacitors in order to ensure the delivery of reliable pulses. The Los Alamos Portable Pulser is a large structure that utilizes a 1.14 MV Marx generator to produce high-voltage electromagnetic pulses, characterized by a rapid risetime of a few nanoseconds. There are 114 total capacitors in use, which are split in groups of 3, for a total of 38 stages. The capacitors are readily available high-voltage “doorknob” capacitors whose dielectric is composed of barium-strontium titanate. During normal operation, the capacitors undergo numerous chargedischarge cycles, ranging from tens to hundreds in a single day. The primary aim of this study is to gain insight into and analyze the mechanisms leading to capacitor failures, specifically focusing on the deterioration of the capacitor's properties and the system performance effects caused by the deterioration. Understanding the underlying mechanisms responsible for the decay of capacitors allows for the development of refined maintenance and calibration schedules, ensuring equipment readiness and the consistent delivery of dependable pulses.

articleTitle: Behavior of Air Insulation at Sub-Atmospheric Pressures Under Negative DC Voltages
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: Rising global temperatures caused by greenhouse gas emissions have accelerated the push toward electrified transportation capable of operating with zero emissions, including the development of all electric aircraft (AEA) by 2050 in the United States. A ± 5 kV bipolar medium voltage direct current (MVDC) architecture is under investigation for use in the electrical power systems (EPS) of all-electric aircraft. The use of high voltages in reduced-pressure environments poses considerable challenges, with partial discharges (PDs) in or on insulation materials being a primary concern. This study investigates the partial discharge behavior of air under negative DC voltage across interelectrode gaps of 1 cm, 2 cm, and 3 cm by conducting experiments in a pressure-controlled laboratory environment, using a needle-to-plane electrode configuration to replicate aviation-relevant conditions. Partial discharge inception voltage (PDIV) and breakdown voltage (BDV) were measured across various pressures for each gap distance, and regression analysis was employed to elucidate their dependence on pressure. Our findings reveal a clear dependence of both partial discharge inception voltage (PDIV) and breakdown voltage (BDV) on pressure and interelectrode gap distance. As the gap increases, both PDIV and BDV rise correspondingly, with their behavior showing noticeable variation across pressure levels. The data exhibits strong second-order polynomial fits with high coefficients of determination, and the rate of increase in BDV is steeper than that of PDIV, particularly at larger gaps, indicating a higher sensitivity of breakdown voltage to pressure changes. These results provide critical insights for designing robust EPS insulation systems for all-electric aircraft, ensuring reliable performance under varying atmospheric conditions. The novel insights gained from this research are essential for the development of reliable and efficient all-electric aircraft, supporting the broader goal of achieving sustainable and zeroemission aviation.

articleTitle: Impact of Mission Profile and Pulse-Width Modulated High Dv/dt Voltage on Aerospace Wiring
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: This paper investigates the impact of pulse width modulation (PWM) voltage waveform, altitude, and temperature conditions on wiring insulation in electric unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). The test methodology, partial discharge (PD) behaviors, thermal imaging and lifetime results for an ETFE wire insulation configuration following SAE AIR 7506 are presented. Thermal analysis identifies the combined dielectric power loss and PD loss under high-frequency, high dv/dt PWM voltage as the main cause of failure. The findings may contribute to the development and improvement of aerospace wire testing standards.

articleTitle: A Review of High Voltage Challenges and Developments of Power Electronics Packaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: Enormous demand for multiple operation scenarios requires structural and material innovations for high-power electronic devices. Several review papers demonstrated the process and advantages of power module packaging around 2020, summarizing the existing problems caused by high switching rate, high voltage isolation, high temperature and thermal management. With the development of the power module packaging, a large number of studies have boomed in the last two years from different research aspects. This paper thoroughly reviews the most recent researches on high voltage challenges and implications from various aspects, including the electric field simulation and experiments, insulation problems under high switching frequency and high slew rate. The promising package cooling process as well as the possible discharge detection and monitoring methods are also exhibited, providing references for wide bandgap (WBG) and ultra-wide bandgap (UWBG) devices.

articleTitle: High-Intensity Pulses Modulate Key Cellular Processes of MDA-MD-468 Human Triple-Negative Breast Cancer Cells Treated With Metformin
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: Human cells and proteins function as biodielectric systems, with cell membranes typically impermeable or less permeable to external molecules, such as chemo drugs, reducing their efficacy. High-intensity, short-duration electric pulses (EP) can create temporary pores in cell membranes, enhancing drug uptake. This study investigates the combined effects of EP and Metformin (Met) on MDA-MB-468, human triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) cells, aiming to discover new treatment strategies. Metformin, a common type- 2 diabetes drug, has shown anticancer potential. We used highthroughput, quantitative, label-free proteomic analysis to evaluate the impact of Met alone and EP + Met at 1 mM and 1000 V/cm. Our results reveal 376 unique proteins in Met, 254 for EP+ Met, and 450 common proteins. Further, Bioinformatics analysis using the Gene Ontology enrichment analysis and visualization tool (GOrilla) indicates that the EP + Met combination targets the electron transport chain (ETC) within mitochondria. These findings suggest that EP and Met modulate key cellular processes in mitochondria, presenting a promising approach for targeted TNBC therapies. The upregulation of the ETC, increased cell death, and EP + Met can be used as a novel, alternate therapeutic strategy to improve outcomes in TNBC patients.

articleTitle: Hold-Off and Nanosecond-Scale Delay Times of C4F7N Electric Breakdown Compared to Other Insulating Gases at Up to 3 Atm Pressure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: The presented work expands the tested pressure regime of C4F7N electric high-voltage pulse breakdown to ~3 atmospheres for tens of nanoseconds pulse applications. Previously, the normalized pulsed electric field vs. breakdown delay time was determined for a variety of gases, such as mixtures of C4F7N, SF6, N2, CO2, between 1 atm and 2 atm. It was found that C4F7N mixtures outperformed SF6 mixtures breakdown hold-off in this pressure region. Gas mixtures of C4F7N with 50% CO2 also exhibited increased breakdown fields when compared to 100% SF6 test in the 1 atm to 2 atm regime. These mixtures also displayed an increased time delay-pressure product compared to 100% SF6.

articleTitle: A Comparison of the Optical Emission Spectra of Insulating Gases During Pulsed Discharge
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: The breakdown behavior of insulating gases above atmospheric pressures and electric fields approaching 1 MV/cm is studied using optical emission spectroscopy. Concern surrounding the environmental impacts of Sulfur Hexafluoride (SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>) has driven significant research into using more environmentally friendly insulating gases to replace SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> for electrical distribution and pulsed power applications. One such gas is the perfluoronitrile Novec™ 4710 (C4F7N), which is capable of twice the DC holdoff voltage of SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> at atmospheric pressure. Optical emission spectroscopy permits observation of the performance of a subject gas during electrical breakdown, offering the ability to identify decomposition products of the gas, as well as their internal energy distribution. In this work, the optical emission spectra of Novec™ 4710, and SF6 under pulsed electrical breakdown are presented and compared at above atmospheric pressures, and an overview of the apparatus used to acquire these spectra is provided. The effects of varying gas pressure and, thus, gap voltage are explored and observed; atomic decomposition products are compared to the available literature.

articleTitle: Upgrading the LCLS-II System to Meet 929 kHz Requirements*
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: The LCLS-II superconducting Linear Accelerator (LINAC) is designed to operate at 929 kHz. Currently, the spreader kicker system operates at 500 kHz, limiting the achievable pulse rate to about half of the design rate. Notable challenges in the prior testing phase included problems with reflection diodes, load resistors, and MOSFETs. This paper delves into these challenges and presents viable solutions. A comprehensive MOSFET and gate-driver selection process is outlined. To validate proposed solutions, a preliminary half-scale experimental test is conducted on the test stand. This considerably simplifies the test stand while allowing focus on full power testing of the MOSFETs. The proposed test plan encompasses the design, construction, and testing of updated driver chassis and PCBs tailored for the integration of new MOSFETs, gate-drivers, and control power supplies. Additional discussion includes results of updated load and reflection diode testing.

articleTitle: A Self-Matching Cable Pulse Generator for High Voltage and Fast Risetime Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: The design and performance of a high voltage and fast risetime cable pulse generator are presented. This pulse generator is intended to enable exploration of the theory that field emission from the insulator serves as a key contributor to the development of anode-initiated flashover. In such an experiment, the load may be approximated as an open circuit gap subjected to high field stress. With an open-circuit load, the transmission line-based pulse generator is capable of delivering a pulse of equal magnitude to its DC charging voltage, while the self-matching topology employed in this generator serves to prevent continuing reflections otherwise caused by the load.

articleTitle: Investigation of Pulsed Nanocrystalline Magnetic Core Behavior
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: This research investigates the behavior of nanocrystalline magnetic cores subject to high magnetization rates in pulsed experiments. The two core materials considered in this work are the nanocrystalline FINEMET™ FT-3KL and FT-3KM. The single and multi-pulse behavior of each core has been examined under high magnetization rates to demonstrate the influence of the magnetization rate on the shape of the hysteresis curve. Based on the measured core behavior, a pulsed magnetic core behavioral simulation model has been developed in LTSpice to provide quick and more accurate results than the conventional LTSpice options. Unlike the default LTSpice saturable core models, this model targets use in pulsed power systems with high magnetization rates. The prevailing feature of this model is the pulsed voltage dependence that captures the experimentally observed hysteresis curve widening effect.

articleTitle: Retrofitted RITS Marx Generator for Laser Triggered Gas Switch Testing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: A Marx generator module from the decommissioned RITS pulsed power machine from Sandia National Labs was modified to operate in an existing setup at Texas Tech University. This will ultimately be used as a testbed for laser triggered gas switching. The existing experimental setup at Texas Tech University consists of a large Marx tank, an oil-filled coaxial pulse forming line, an adjustable peaking gap, and load section along with various diagnostics. The setup was previously operated at a lower voltage than the new experiment, so electrostatic modeling was done to ensure viability and drive needed modifications. The oil tank will house the modified RITS Marx. This Marx contains half as many stages as the original RITS module and has an expected output of 1 MV. A trigger Marx generator consisting of 8 stages has been fabricated to trigger the RITS Marx. Charging and triggering of both Marx generators will be controlled through a fiber optic network. The output from the modified RITS Marx will be used to charge the oil-filled coaxial line acting as a low impedance pulse forming line (PFL). Once charged, the self-breaking peaking gap will close, allowing the compressed pulse to be released into the load section. For testing of the Marx module and PFL, a match 10 Ω water load was fabricated. The output pulsewidth is ~ 55 nsec. Diagnostics include two capacitive voltage probes on either side of the peaking gap, a quarter-turn Rogowski coil for load current measurement, and a Pearson coil for calibrations purposes.

articleTitle: The Influence of Low Pressure on Dielectric Strength of Aircraft MVDC Power Cable
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: The electrification of transportation systems has emerged as a key component in achieving net-zero emission goals, leading to widespread adoption within the transportation sector. As a result of this rapid expansion, the aviation industry is also moving towards all-electric aircraft (AEA). An electric power system (EPS) with high power delivery and low system mass is essential for AEA. Cables play a crucial role in this future EPS, and one approach to reducing cable weight is to operate at a higher voltage. However, designing insulation systems for higher voltages is challenging due to the increased partial discharge (PD) activity in adverse aviation environments characterized by extremely low pressures and moisture. The development of multilayer multifunction electrical insulation (MMEI) systems has addressed these issues by providing higher breakdown strength compared to single-layer insulation systems. In our previous work, we designed several MMEI-based medium voltage direct current (MVDC) power cables (±5 kV) capable of operating at low pressures of 18.8 kPa, corresponding to an altitude of 12.2 km, which is the typical cruising altitude of wide-body aircraft, through modeling and simulation. This paper presents the experimental studies of the selected ARC-SC-T-MMEI design. The samples are manufactured, and their dielectric strength under DC voltage is tested at both atmospheric and low pressure. Additionally, the behavior of the insulation's dielectric strength under low-pressure conditions is investigated.

articleTitle: Development of a Circuit Modeling Capability for Semiconductor Opening Switch-Based Pulsed Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: Semiconductor opening switches (SOSs) are crucial for compact, solid-state pulsed power systems, yet their quantitative and predictive capabilities remain limited. This restricts the optimization of pulsed power generators using SOS devices. This study aims to develop a semi-empirical model of SOS devices for circuit modeling using SPICE simulation software. An existing SOS device is experimentally characterized using a pulse generator system capable of 200 kV pulses with sub-20 ns rise times and a 100 Hz repetition rate. The experimental results, combined with particle swarm optimization, guide the develonment of a simnle SOS device model.

articleTitle: Compact, Repetitive Nanosecond Pulse Generation for Industrial Applications: the Advance of the Solid-State Impedance Matched Marx Generator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: In this contribution we will present our work on fast, compact, repetitive, high-voltage nanosecond pulse generation for industrial applications at Eindhoven University of Technology. We mainly focus on our work on the solid-state Impedance-matched Marx Generator (IMG). Based on the topology of the IMG presented in 2017 by researchers from Sandia (and others), we created a solid-state IMG using MOSFET switches. The advantage of using the IMG topology is that by using transmission lines to transmit the pulses from the Marx stages, the rise time of the pulses can be maintained at the output waveform (when carefully impedance-matched). By designing the Marx stages very compactly and using fast semiconductor components, adjustable pulses with rise times of just several nanoseconds are feasible with this topology. Since we require such fast rising pulses for transient plasma generation, the solid-state IMG is ideally suited for our purpose. In this contribution we present our prototypes thus far (going up to 30 kV) - including plasma experiments with those sources - and our plans for >100kV versions, together with the topic of flexible pulse generation in large generators. For such large generators, the physical size of the generator becomes detrimental to flexible pulse generation (because this violates one of the matching criteria). Beyond presenting the state-of-the-art, we will present future research lines on three different versions of the solid-state IMG at voltage levels of 200 kV, 300 kV and 700 kV.

articleTitle: Design and Operation of a High Rep-Rate, Solid-State Switched, Bipolar Spiral Generator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Power Modulator and High Voltage Conference (IPMHVC)
abstract: Spiral generators are pulsed-power devices than can produce high-voltage pulses in an ultra-compact form factor. The spiral generator is charged at a lower DC voltage and a single switch shorts one end of the spiral stripline. The result is a highvoltage pulse on the order of hundreds of nanoseconds in width. Historically, spark gaps were used as the shorting switches. While beneficial for voltage holdoff capability, this prohibits reaching high pulse repetition frequencies (PRF) or the use in jitter sensitive applications. Previous work has demonstrated high repetition rate operation of a single-ended spiral generator using Silicon-Carbide (SiC) transistors as the spiral generator closing switch, which resulted in demonstrated PRF of 100 kHz at output voltage near 10 kV. This work will describe the advancement of solid-state spiral generator architecture to a bipolar system which converts a 1.2 kV input charge to 44 kV peak-to-peak pulses with sub- 10 ns risetime at 100 kHz PRF with pulse-to-pulse jitter of 160 ps. Commentary on the solid-state switching architecture, bipolar spiral generators, and resulting operation is presented.
